- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.6), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction: if price spikes, forecast next period should be slightly lower than peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 20% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period rallies; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive and price has been trending up.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 1.00), model tends to misalign with sentiment cycles; adjust forecast to match sentiment direction in 3–5 day window.
